report.headline: Usage projected to compress toward NBA average (19.2%) from a EuroLeague usage 0.84 SD above league mean; efficiency projection carries no reliable signal

projection.text: Projected NBA usage rate is 19.2%, close to the league average of 20.0% and down from the subject's EuroLeague usage of 23.9%, which sat 0.84 standard deviations above that league's mean; the EL->NBA usage slope of 0.575 indicates only about 57.5% of a player's above-league standing typically carries into the NBA.

risks.text: Projected NBA usage of 19.2% falls below the subject's EuroLeague usage of 23.9% and just under the receiving league's 20.0% average, reflecting the typical role compression seen when players move from Europe to the NBA.

The 80% interval for usage (14.0%-24.4%) spans a range nearly two NBA usage standard deviations (5.3%) wide, meaning the model situates this player relative to peers but does not forecast a precise usage figure.

The true shooting projection of 54.4% should not be relied upon: the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than simply predicting the league average (4.3%), so this metric carries no reliable signal for this transition.
Turnover rate in the source season was 16.3%, a cost that accompanied the high assist and usage numbers and may compound in a higher-talent environment.

strengths.text: In the EuroLeague source season the subject posted a 31.4% assist rate and 6.004 assists per 75 possessions, playmaking numbers that accompanied a usage rate 0.84 standard deviations above the league average (23.9% usage).
Shooting efficiency was well above the EuroLeague norm, with a 61.2% true shooting percentage sitting 0.66 standard deviations above the league mean.
The scoring diet leaned heavily on the three-point line, with 51.9% of shot attempts taken from three.

The historical cohort of 61 EL->NBA movers used to fit this estimate already sat 0.46 standard deviations above their own league's average, consistent with the subject's above-average source-season profile.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs 14.0%-24.4% and the 95% interval 11.3%-27.2%, spans of roughly 2 to 3 standard deviations of the NBA usage distribution (5.3%), so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot pin an individual outcome; the true shooting projection of 54.4% is less trustworthy still, since its out-of-fold error (4.5%) is worse than simply guessing the league average (4.3%).
